Cover memo

↑ Contents

This record documents the website accessibility program for [[site]] ([[Client, and the brands or parent company the site covers]]), which began with a baseline audit on [[Month D, YYYY]]. It is maintained by Accessrank, Inc. and refreshed on request. Every item is dated, and every finding is measured against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA.

The record is organized so a reader can answer three questions quickly: what the client knew and when, what has been fixed and when, and what the client is doing on an ongoing basis. Section 1 establishes the starting point. Sections 2 and 3 show the fixes and the current state of conformance. Sections 4 through 7 show whether the program is public, continuous, human-verified and committed. Accessrank can regenerate any section with current data on request; contact [[Account lead name]], Accessrank account lead, [[account lead email]], [[phone]].

This record is a draft. It is not issued until [[Client]] has approved the Accessibility Statement and Footer packet in the client portal. That packet settles three things this record cannot state until then: the wording of the public accessibility statement, the accessibility contact and reply time the statement will name, and whether the Accessrank footer block is published. Every point in this record that depends on those answers is marked [like this] and will be completed from the returned packet, after which the record is issued, the attestation forms are signed, and the version becomes 1.0.[[Client]] answered the Accessibility Statement and Footer packet in the client portal: [signer and date]. The approved statement, the accessibility contact and reply time, and the footer decision are recorded in Section 4 and Section 7, and each point in this record that depended on them is completed from those answers.

What the proposed statement claims

It claims no conformance. It says that WCAG 2.2 Level AA is the target, describes what has actually been done — automated scanning plus Accessrank staff review — and lists the known limits, including that manual testing with assistive-technology users [[is under way / is planned]] and that third-party and platform-hosted pages sit outside the work. It makes no claim that the site has been tested with VoiceOver, NVDA or JAWS unless it has been.

When manual testing with assistive technology is done, the statement will be updated with the results (Section 6). Only after that testing, and only for the pages and date tested, can it say the site conforms to WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Recommended wording until then: “we aim to conform to WCAG 2.2 AA, and we know of the limits listed in this record”, not “the site conforms”.

↑ Contents

[[Status: not started / in progress / completed, and with which assistive technology]]. Automated scanning cannot confirm every WCAG criterion. Manual testing and testing with assistive technology, such as screen readers and keyboard-only use, checks things a scan cannot, for example whether a page makes sense when read aloud and whether the shopping path can be completed without a mouse. Accessibility Statement

[[Client, and the brands it covers]] wants everyone to be able to shop and read on [[site]]. We are working to make the site usable with a keyboard, a screen reader, zoom, and other assistive tools.

Our goal

Our target is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, Level AA, an international standard for accessible websites. This is a goal we are working toward. We are not claiming the site fully meets it.

What we have done

We had the site audited for accessibility barriers. Between [[Month]] and [[Month D, YYYY]], we fixed what the audit found, working in the site’s code and content with our Accessibility & Discovery services partner, Accessrank.ai. Fixes include:

  • [[plain-language fix, e.g. Text descriptions for banner, slideshow and product images]]
  • [[plain-language fix]]

We fix problems in the site’s own code. We do not use an accessibility overlay or widget to cover them up.

How we test

We scan the site with automated testing tools, and Accessrank.ai staff review the items that need a judgement call, such as image descriptions and text over photos. On [[Month D, YYYY]], automated testing found [[result]] on the [[pages]]. Automated tools find only part of the possible problems.

Known limitations

  • We are conducting manual testing with people who use assistive technology, such as screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA and JAWS), keyboard-only navigation and screen magnification, including on phones. We will update this accessibility statement when that testing is complete.
  • [[platform-hosted pages, e.g. Checkout, Shop Pay and customer account pages are provided by Shopify and are outside the review described above.]]
  • Some features come from other companies, such as [[third-party apps and widgets]]. We have fixed the problems we found in how they appear on our site and report issues to their providers, but we cannot guarantee how they behave when those providers update them.

Tell us if you have trouble

If you cannot use part of [[site]], or you need information in another form, please contact [the contact the client approves in the portal]. You can also write to [[Client]] at [[business mailing address]].If you cannot use part of [[site]], or you need information in another form, please contact us at [email] or [phone].
